title: The unimodality conjecture for Euclid polynomials
statement: Let $E_k(\lambda)$ be the Euclid polynomials. A polynomial $p(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}a_j\lambda^j$ is **unimodal** when its coefficient vector $[a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ consists of positive integers that first increases monotonically to a peak, possibly attained at two or more adjacent coefficients, and then decreases monotonically to $a_n=1$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The Euclid polynomials are unimodal. The first four Euclid polynomials are stated to have this property, but no general proof or resolution is supplied in the provided text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04405

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).
source_name: Eunice Y. S. Chan and Robert M. Corless, “Minimal height companion matrices for Euclid polynomials”, arXiv:1712.04405 (2017).
